thread:
mia: quick heads-up — I noticed the consent-bridge path will accept older consent tokens and create an inspect allowlist entry without re-checking tenant-level 'inspect_enabled' flag. could cause unredacted captures slipping through :grimacing:

sam: ah damn. where in the flow? request proxy -> consent-bridge -> inspector?

mia: yeah. sequence is: proxy validates token, consent-bridge issues ephemeral allowlist id (ttl default 24h), and inspector uses allowlist id to bypass scrubbing. no extra tenant feature check.

anita: that sounds risky. we intended the allowlist to be gated by tenant preference. is the token validation verifying signature only?

mia: exactly — signature only. long-lived tokens signed by 3rd-party SSO can be replayed.

leo: quick mitigation: check tenant record at allowlist creation time and at inspector fetch. cheap read on creation, and a short-circuit guard on inspector.

sam: agree. also TTL should be short by default. 24h is too long for bypass list. propose 15m default, configurable per-tenant.

anita: +1 on 15m. plus audit entry on every allowlist create + every inspector accept. we need traceability if something leaks.

mia: prototype config sketch:

```
# consent-bridge config
allowlist_ttl_seconds: 900  # 15m
require_tenant_optin_on_create: true
audit_backfill_queue: enabled
```

leo: FYI ops-bot just ran the canary with old tokens and it did create entries. ops-bot: "consent-bridge canary created allowlist id=alb_9x7; tenant=acme-corp; token_age_days=90"

ops-bot: incident-note: temporary block applied to canary, rollback triggered for consent-bridge v2.

sam: question: if we start enforcing require_tenant_optin_on_create=true, will any existing customer workflows break? needs product heads sign-off.

anita: we should run an impact query: count allowlist creates by tenant in last 30d and cross-ref to tenant.inspect_enabled. can someone run it?

mia: on it. running now; rough sql: `select tenant_id, count(*) from allowlist_creates where created_at > now() - interval '30 days' group by tenant_id;`

leo: add to that: show token_age buckets so we can see replay risk.

sam: UX question — if we block creation due to opt-in=false, what should the console show when a user clicks "inspect"? Options: (1) greyed out with tooltip, (2) prompt to request audit access, (3) show masked preview and a request button.

anita: prefer (2) + audit email. we need a product flow so customers don't hit silent failures.

mia: also need dashboard metrics: allowlist_create_rate, allowlist_accept_rate, avg_ttl, token_age_histogram, and per-tenant failed_create_reasons.

leo: operationally we need quota rules: creating allowlists counts against tenant debug quota (so noisy customers can't exhaust). if they hit quota, fallback to masked previews.

sam: can we reuse existing debug quota buckets? yes but ensure UI communicates quota consumption when user requests inspect.

anita: final ask before we change prod: add inspector guard at fetch time (double-check tenant opt-in) and short TTL default. then product can decide if they want to opt-in to longer.

mia: plan: patch consent-bridge to consult tenant flag during create, set default ttl 15m, add audit events, and add inspector guard. will open PR and tag @sam @anita for product/ops review.

sam: thx. please include migration plan for existing allowlists: auto-expire any >1h and notify tenants with >0 active allowlists that we will tighten defaults.

leo: ops will create a dashboard alert for sudden spikes in allowlist_create_rate.

anita: +1 for notification cadence and a short RFC note for audit. also add a unit test that rejects creation when tenant opt-in=false unless override flag `force_by_support` is present.

mia: will send PR link and a brief RFC summary in #eng-platform when ready.

ops-bot: scheduled task created: notify-tenants-with-legacy-allowlists @ 2026-04-01T08:00:00Z

sam: nice. thanks team :thumbsup:
